title: Almost One Bit Violation of Minimum-Output Rényi Entropy Additivity Simultaneously at All Orders
authors: Guocheng Zhen, Chengkai Zhu, Ranyiliu Chen, Xin Wang
abstract: We prove that minimum-output Rényi-entropy additivity can fail by almost one bit simultaneously at every nonnegative order. For every $\varepsilon\in(0,\log2)$, there exists a finite-dimensional quantum channel with a real Stinespring isometry such that the same maximally entangled input witnesses a tensor-square entropy gap of at least $\log2-\varepsilon$ for all $p\in[0,\infty]$. The output dimension can be chosen to be $O(\varepsilon^{-3})$ as $\varepsilon\downarrow0$.   The construction uses direct products of free groups: tensorized Haagerup estimates control the one-copy outputs, while commutation between distinct factors forces exact Bell-branch collisions at two copies. Strong convergence gives both an existential realization through finite-dimensional representations of right-angled Artin groups followed by realification, and a Haar-orthogonal model whose success probability tends to one as the matrix dimension grows. We also determine the exact Bell quotient, prove asymptotically sharp regular-radius bounds, and show that the cubic output-dimension scale is optimal within the present purity--rank certificate.
summary: This paper establishes a strong counterexample demonstrating that the minimum-output Rényi entropy is not additive for quantum channels. By constructing a specific quantum channel based on free group structures, the authors prove that the entropy fails to be additive by almost one bit simultaneously for all possible Rényi orders. This result significantly impacts the theoretical understanding of quantum information measures.
main_problem: The paper investigates the additivity property of the minimum-output Rényi entropy for quantum channels, aiming to prove a simultaneous violation across all non-negative orders.
main_result: It proves that the minimum-output Rényi entropy can fail to be additive by an amount approaching one full bit ($\log 2 - \epsilon$) simultaneously for all orders $p \in [0, \infty)$.
method: The proof constructs a counterexample using quantum channels derived from the direct product of free groups, leveraging tensorized Haagerup estimates and group theory constructions.
model_or_system: The model is a quantum channel $\Phi$ acting on a finite-dimensional system, whose structure is derived from the direct product of free groups, $G_{r,d} =  igotimes_{j=1}^{r} F(j)^d$.
key_observables: The primary observable is the entropy gap, $\Delta\Omega_p(\Phi) = 2H_{\min,p}(\Phi) - H_p(\Phi^{\otimes 2}|\Omega_mangle\langle\Omega_m|)$, which is shown to remain large.
important_parameters: The violation gap is $\log 2 - \epsilon$, and the required output dimension scales as $O(\epsilon^{-3})$ as $\epsilon 	o 0$.
main_assumptions: The construction relies on strong convergence results for representations of right-angled Artin groups and the use of specific group structures to enforce the non-additivity.

paper_structure: The paper builds the counterexample by relating the entropy gap to one-copy purity and two-copy information, combining tools from operator algebras and free probability to establish the simultaneous violation across the entire Rényi spectrum.
why_interesting: This work provides a fundamental theoretical counterexample to an additivity conjecture in quantum information theory, which has implications for understanding the fundamental limits of quantum channel capacity and entanglement measures.
